newsitem.title: USA: Gas well blowout in gulf forces rig crew to flee.
newsitem.headline: Gas well blowout in gulf forces rig crew to flee.

text.p: A natural gas well blowout in the Gulf of Mexico forced 39 people to abandon a drilling rig where they were rescued by a private vessel, the Coast Guard said on Monday.
The cause of the blowout, which took place on Saturday night about 40 miles (64 km) off the coast southeast of Cameron, Louisiana, was under investigation.

Well operator Houston Exploration Co said in a statement that no one was injured in the accident. The workers escaped in a rescue capsule, which is standard equipment on offshore rigs, and were picked up by the vessel Seabulk Aransas, the Coast Guard said.
A Coast Guard spokesman said natural gas was spewing from the ruptured rig but there had been no fire or oil spills.

A Houston Exploration spokesman said the well was expected to produce six million to eight million cubic feet (226,500 cubic metres) of gas a day. A team from Wild Well Control Inc. of Houston was on the scene working to cap the blowout.
